Amazon CloudWatch Network Monitor probes

Subscribe to AWS Security Incident Response and connect it to the organization so it triages findings, opens cases, and engages the AWS CIRT
Configure AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager response plans that page the AWS CIRT through an escalation plan for every finding

stem: A team built an EventBridge rule for GuardDuty EC2 findings that invokes a Lambda function to tag the instance, swap its security group, and snapshot its volumes. They must prove the whole chain works against a real instance in a test account before production. Which test approach fits?

choices.text: Deploy the amazon-guardduty-tester environment in the test account so real activity from a test instance creates genuine findings for that instance
Import a custom finding into Security Hub with BatchImportFindings that names the test instance, so the GuardDuty rule receives it as a finding
Run the EventBridge TestEventPattern API with a saved GuardDuty finding, so the rule invokes the function against the test instance end to end
Call the GuardDuty CreateSampleFindings API for the EC2 finding types so the rule fires and the function isolates the instance named in the finding

stem: An incident response runbook for compromised EC2 instances says: isolate the instance, snapshot all EBS volumes, then stop the instance. In a drill, analysts found that the simulated malware ran only in memory and left no trace on the volumes. How should the runbook change?

choices.text: Enable VPC Traffic Mirroring on the instance before stopping it, so memory contents are copied to the mirror target for later analysis
Enable GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring, because each runtime finding includes a full memory dump of the process that triggered it
Take multi-volume snapshots with crash-consistent mode enabled, because that mode writes the instance's memory pages into the snapshot
Before stopping, use Systems Manager Run Command to run a pre-staged memory acquisition tool and write the image to the forensics bucket

stem: A company stores forensic disk images and memory captures in an S3 bucket in its forensics account. Legal requires that no one, including administrators of that account and its root user, can delete or overwrite any evidence object for one year after upload. Which configuration meets this requirement?

choices.text: Enable versioning with S3 Object Lock and a default retention of one year in governance mode on the evidence bucket
Enable versioning with MFA Delete so that deleting any object version requires the root user and its MFA device code
Enable versioning with S3 Object Lock and a default retention of one year in compliance mode on the evidence bucket
Enable versioning and apply a legal hold to every uploaded object, removing each hold one year after its upload date

stem: A workforce user in AWS IAM Identity Center is suspected of being compromised. The user has active AWS access portal sessions and has already obtained role credentials in several accounts through permission sets with a 4-hour session duration. Which TWO actions stop this user's access as quickly as possible? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Remove the permission set assignments for the user, which immediately revokes the role credentials already issued
Delete the AWSReservedSSO roles in each affected account so Identity Center must recreate them for every user
Reset the user's password in IAM Identity Center, which also invalidates all role credentials already issued to it
Add a deny statement to the user's permission sets that matches the user's session name in the aws:userid key
Disable the user in the identity source and delete the user's active sessions in the IAM Identity Center console

stem: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring reports a cryptocurrency miner running in one pod of an Amazon EKS deployment that uses the Amazon VPC CNI with network policy enabled. The team must stop the pod's network activity while keeping the pod and node intact for forensic analysis. What should the responder do first?

choices.text: Label the pod, apply a deny-all ingress and egress NetworkPolicy that selects that label, and cordon the worker node
Delete the pod so the deployment controller replaces it with a fresh copy, and then snapshot the node's root volume
Attach a security group with no rules to the worker node's primary network interface, and then terminate the affected pod
Scale the deployment to zero replicas so the miner stops, and then review the container image for the infection source

stem: GuardDuty reports UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS for the IAM role used by a web server fleet. The team finds a server-side request forgery flaw in the web application that lets attackers fetch URLs from the instance. Which TWO actions contain this incident and block the attack path? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable GuardDuty S3 Protection on the account, which blocks API calls that use EC2 role credentials from outside AWS
Require IMDSv2 on the fleet by setting HttpTokens to required, so metadata requests need a session token from a PUT request
Detach and reattach the instance profile on each instance, which invalidates the temporary credentials already issued to it
Rotate the role's access keys in the IAM console, which invalidates the keys the attacker copied from the instance metadata
Revoke the role's active sessions, which adds a deny for credentials whose aws:TokenIssueTime is older than the revocation time

stem: On-premises servers use IAM Roles Anywhere with a trust anchor that points to the company's own certificate authority. A server's private key was stolen, so the security team revoked its certificate at the CA and published an updated CRL at the CRL distribution point. The stolen certificate can still obtain AWS credentials. What must the team do?

choices.text: Turn on OCSP checking for the trust anchor so IAM Roles Anywhere queries the CA's responder before issuing each set of credentials
Replace the CRL distribution point in the certificate with a public HTTPS URL that IAM Roles Anywhere is able to fetch on each request
Update the IAM Roles Anywhere profile's session duration to 15 minutes so that the credentials of the revoked certificate expire sooner
Import the updated certificate revocation list into IAM Roles Anywhere with the ImportCrl API and enable it for the trust anchor

stem: A consumer app uses an Amazon Cognito user pool for email and password sign-in. Credential stuffing attacks are rising. Without writing custom code, the company wants to block sign-ins that use passwords known from public breaches and require MFA only when a sign-in looks risky. Which TWO settings meet this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Configure a password policy with history and 14 characters, which rejects passwords known from breached credential lists
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the user pool and add a rate-based rule, which also blocks known breached passwords
Enable threat protection on a Plus plan user pool and configure adaptive authentication to require MFA at higher risk
Add a pre token generation Lambda trigger that inspects the risk level and requires MFA before the tokens are issued
Enable threat protection on a Plus plan user pool and turn on compromised credentials detection to block the sign-in

stem: An organization has 300 member accounts, each with its own root user password and MFA device stored in a safe. The security team wants to remove long-term root credentials from member accounts but still be able to fix an S3 bucket policy that accidentally denies all principals. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Enable centralized root access management, delete member root credentials, and use sts:AssumeRoot with the S3UnlockBucketPolicy task policy
Keep the root passwords but replace each MFA device with a passkey stored in a shared vault that only the security team members can open
Create an IAM Identity Center permission set with AdministratorAccess and assign it in every account to remove locked bucket policies
Attach an SCP that denies all actions by the root user in member accounts, and use an administrator role to edit the locked bucket policy

stem: A platform team runs 60 Amazon EKS clusters and uses IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA). Each new cluster requires another IAM OIDC provider and edits to trust policies that are nearing their size limit. The team wants pods to keep per-service-account roles with less setup per cluster. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Attach one broad role to every node's instance profile, and let pods read credentials from the node's instance metadata
Move to EKS Pod Identity, with role trust policies for pods.eks.amazonaws.com and associations of roles to service accounts
Share one IAM OIDC provider across all clusters by adding each cluster's issuer URL as another client ID on that provider
Store long-term access keys for each service account in Secrets Manager and mount them into pods with the CSI driver

stem: Developers federate from a SAML identity provider into a role, then chain into deployment roles in other accounts and choose their own role session names. Auditors require CloudTrail to show the corporate username for every action, including after role chaining, and developers must not be able to change or remove it. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Pass the SourceIdentity SAML attribute from the IdP and allow sts:SetSourceIdentity in the trust policies of the federated and deployment roles
Use CloudTrail Lake to join AssumeRole events by access key ID, rebuilding the chain from each deployment session back to the federated user
Require developers to set RoleSessionName to their corporate username with a condition on sts:RoleSessionName in every deployment role
Add the username as a non-transitive session tag at federation, so every chained role session carries the tag in its CloudTrail records

stem: A data lake bucket holds folders for 400 corporate groups. Users and groups come from Microsoft Entra ID through IAM Identity Center. Each group needs read or read-write access to its own prefixes, the bucket policy is near its size limit, and CloudTrail must show which corporate user accessed the data. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Create one S3 access point per group, each with a policy that grants the Identity Center group ARN access to that group's prefix
Create an S3 Access Grants instance linked to IAM Identity Center and add grants that map each directory group to its prefix and access level
Create one IAM role per group with a prefix policy, and have users assume the role that matches their group through access keys
Add one statement per group to the bucket policy that uses the aws:PrincipalTag key to match each user's group tag against the prefix name

stem: A security team attaches a resource control policy (RCP) to all OUs that denies s3:* unless aws:PrincipalOrgID equals the organization ID. Soon after, the organization CloudTrail trail and AWS Config stop delivering files to the central logging bucket in a member account. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Replace the RCP with an SCP that has the same deny statement, because SCPs apply to all principals that call the bucket's APIs
Attach the RCP to the management account instead of the OUs, because RCPs in the management account exclude service principals
Add a BoolIfExists condition on aws:PrincipalIsAWSService set to false to the RCP deny, so calls by AWS service principals are exempt
Add statements to the logging bucket policy that allow cloudtrail.amazonaws.com and config.amazonaws.com to put objects there

stem: A document service uses one IAM role for all tenants. For each request it calls AssumeRole with an inline session policy allowing s3:* on arn:aws:s3:::docs/tenant-42/*. The role's identity policy allows only s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::docs/*. Uploads from the session fail with AccessDenied. Why?

choices.text: The session policy's prefix is narrower than the role's resource, and a narrower session scope causes STS to deny every write action
The session policy must be passed as a managed policy ARN, because inline session policies are limited to read actions like GetObject
Session policies only apply to credentials from AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, so the AssumeRole call ignored the passed session policy
Session permissions are the intersection of the role's identity policy and the session policy, and the role never allows s3:PutObject

stem: An analytics role reads objects from an S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS using a customer managed key. The security team wants the role to decrypt with that key only when S3 makes the request on its behalf, so the role cannot call KMS Decrypt directly on data copied elsewhere. Which policy condition fits?

choices.text: Allow kms:Decrypt on the key only when the kms:ViaService condition equals s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Allow kms:Decrypt on the key only when aws:CalledVia contains kms.amazonaws.com as the first service called
Allow kms:Decrypt on the key only when aws:PrincipalIsAWSService is true for the request made by the role
Allow kms:Decrypt on the key only when aws:SourceVpce equals the S3 gateway endpoint that the role uses

stem: Developers can create Lambda functions and must attach existing execution roles to them. A review found a developer launched an EC2 instance with a highly privileged role to escalate privileges. Execution roles for Lambda live under the IAM path /lambda-exec/. Which policy change prevents this while still allowing the developers' work?

choices.text: Allow iam:PassRole on all roles, and add an SCP that denies ec2:RunInstances for every developer in the account
Allow iam:PassRole only when aws:RequestedRegion matches the approved Regions where Lambda functions are deployed
Allow iam:PassRole only on roles under /lambda-exec/ with an iam:PassedToService condition of lambda.amazonaws.com
Allow iam:PassRole on all roles, and attach a permissions boundary to each Lambda execution role in the account

stem: A company wants to stop employees from copying corporate data to S3 buckets in personal AWS accounts using their corporate credentials, whether from inside AWS or from on-premises through the VPC endpoints. Which TWO controls establish this resource perimeter? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An RCP that denies s3:PutObject on all buckets unless aws:PrincipalOrgID matches, applied to every OU in the organization
Bucket policies on every corporate bucket that deny access unless aws:PrincipalOrgID equals the organization ID for each request
A GuardDuty S3 Protection configuration that blocks object uploads to buckets that belong to accounts outside the organization
VPC endpoint policies for S3 that allow access only when aws:ResourceOrgID equals the organization ID, with required exceptions
An SCP that denies S3 actions when aws:ResourceOrgID does not equal the organization ID, with exceptions for required AWS-owned buckets

stem: A platform team's pipeline deploys IAM policies from CloudFormation templates. It must fail the build when a changed policy grants more access than the approved version in the main branch, or when any policy allows iam:PassRole or s3:DeleteBucket. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Run the IAM policy simulator against every template in the pipeline and fail the build when any simulated request returns an explicit deny
Run IAM Access Analyzer custom policy checks in the pipeline: CheckNoNewAccess against the approved policy and CheckAccessNotGranted for the actions
Enable an AWS Config rule with the iam-policy-no-statements-with-admin-access check and roll back the stack when the rule reports noncompliance
Run IAM Access Analyzer policy generation in the pipeline and fail the build when the generated policy differs from the one in the template

stem: A company builds container images in AWS CodeBuild and pushes them to Amazon ECR, where Amazon Inspector scans them. The security team now wants the build itself to fail when an image has critical vulnerabilities, before the image is ever pushed to a registry. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Enable ECR enhanced scanning with continuous scan frequency on the repository, and let the build wait for the scan to finish on push
Generate an SBOM of the image in the build with the Inspector SBOM generator and call the Inspector ScanSbom API, failing on critical results
Configure an ECR lifecycle policy that expires images with critical findings, so vulnerable images are removed before they can be deployed
Enable Inspector Lambda code scanning on the CodeBuild project, so the build container's image layers are scanned during each build run

stem: A CloudFormation template for an RDS for PostgreSQL instance takes the master password from a NoEcho parameter whose default value is committed to Git. The security team wants no password in templates, parameter files, or the repository. Which TWO changes meet this goal? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Keep the NoEcho parameter but move its default value to the template's Metadata section, which NoEcho also masks
Encode the password with Fn::Base64 in the template's Mappings section so the plaintext value never appears in Git
Create an AWS::SecretsManager::Secret with GenerateSecretString and reference it with a secretsmanager dynamic reference
Keep the NoEcho parameter and enable SSE-KMS on the S3 bucket that CloudFormation uses to store uploaded templates
Set ManageMasterUserPassword to true on the DB instance so RDS generates the password and stores it in Secrets Manager

stem: A company wants all accounts in its organization to enforce IMDSv2 as the default for new instances and block public sharing of AMIs and EBS snapshots. The settings must remain enforced even if EC2 adds new APIs later, account administrators must not be able to change them, and users should see a custom error message. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Deploy AWS Config conformance packs with automatic remediation that re-enables IMDSv2 and removes public sharing whenever a change is detected
Use CloudFormation StackSets to set the account-level EC2 settings in every account and Region, and redeploy them through an EventBridge schedule
Enable AWS Control Tower detective controls for IMDSv2 and public snapshots, and assign the SOC to fix each noncompliant resource that is reported
Attach EC2 declarative policies in AWS Organizations for instance metadata defaults, image block public access, and snapshot block public access

stem: AWS sent an abuse report about a member account to the account's original owner, who left the company, and nobody on the security team saw it. The organization has 250 member accounts. Which approach makes sure AWS security notifications reach the SOC for every account with the least effort?

choices.text: Enable trusted access for AWS Account Management and call PutAlternateContact with type SECURITY for each member account from the management account
Subscribe the SOC's shared email distribution list to the AWS security bulletins feed so it receives every notice that AWS publishes
Configure AWS User Notifications in the management account to send every Security Hub finding to the SOC email distribution list
Change the root user email address of every member account to the SOC distribution list by signing in as each account's root user one at a time

stem: A company uses AWS Security Hub CSPM in 150 accounts across 4 Regions. Today each account owner decides which standards and controls are enabled. The security team wants one place to enable the CIS benchmark and FSBP standards for production OUs, disable selected controls for sandbox OUs, and stop account owners from changing it. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Use central configuration from the delegated administrator's home Region and associate configuration policies with the OUs
Create an SCP that denies securityhub:BatchDisableStandards in all OUs and then enable the standards in each account manually
Deploy a CloudFormation StackSet that enables the standards in every account and every Region, and then re-run it each week
Enable automatic enablement of default standards in organization settings and ask sandbox owners to disable controls manually

stem: An auditor asks the security team for a list of every unencrypted EBS volume in all 80 accounts and 6 Regions of the organization, with account ID and Region, produced from one place. AWS Config is already recording in every account and Region. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Create an AWS Resource Explorer aggregator index and search the default view for all EBS volumes where the encryption flag is false
Create an organization aggregator in the delegated administrator account and run an advanced query filtered on unencrypted EBS volumes
Configure Systems Manager Inventory with a resource data sync for all accounts and query the synced data for unencrypted volumes
Enable Amazon Inspector for the organization and export the list of EBS volumes that Inspector reports as unencrypted resources
